summary: SteerVAD proposes a tuning-free video anomaly detection framework that intervenes on the internal representations of a frozen MLLM by (1) identifying discriminative attention heads via a Fisher-like separability criterion (RSA) and (2) dynamically modulating their feature vectors via a lightweight FiLM-style hierarchical controller (HMC). The data-efficiency story is well-told, ablations are structured, and the stability analysis is a genuine methodological strength. However, the performance improvements over the strongest tuning-free baseline are narrow (~0.4–0.9%) and their statistical significance is never demonstrated; the technical components are individually known; evaluation is confined to two benchmarks and a single backbone; and the limitations section is generic boilerplate that does not engage honestly with these gaps.
strengths: The motivation to move from passive feature reading to active geometric intervention within a frozen MLLM is clear and well-motivated relative to the cited literature on representational bias and contextual ambiguity.

The calibration stability experiment (Table 3 — 10 independent seed runs, identical LAE selection every time, AUC σ ≈ 0.04%) is a strong empirical signal that the identified functional circuits are intrinsic model properties rather than calibration artifacts.

The data-efficiency analysis (Table 4) is rigorous and honest: the plateau from 1% to 100% training data is quantified explicitly, and the training time cost is disclosed, making the efficiency trade-off concrete and reproducible.

The ablation structure (Table 2, Parts A and B) is well-organized, isolating each component (GSG, LGM, anisotropic vs. additive steering, RSA vs. positional heuristics) with a single-variable-at-a-time discipline.

key_concerns.issue: Statistical significance of the main results is not demonstrated. The margins over the two strongest tuning-free baselines (VERA, HiProbeVAD) are 0.43% AUC on UCF-Crime and 0.87% AP on XD-Violence. No error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported for Table 1, and the seed stability analysis (Table 3) covers only UCF-Crime. Given that HiProbeVAD appears to be an anonymized citation from the same author group ('[Author] et al., 2025'), the effective improvement over the authors' own prior work may be statistically indistinguishable from noise.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report mean ± std over at least 5 seeds for all main Table 1 comparisons. Apply a paired t-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank test against the two strongest baselines and report p-values. Extend the stability analysis to XD-Violence.

key_concerns.issue: Evaluation breadth is insufficient to support generality claims. Results are presented for exactly two benchmarks (UCF-Crime, XD-Violence) and a single MLLM backbone (InternVL3). The paper's framing — 'a powerful new direction for VAD' and 'a promising way against expensive fine-tuning' — implies broader applicability that is not empirically grounded.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Include at least one additional VAD benchmark (e.g., ShanghaiTech or TAD) and, ideally, demonstrate that the RSA + HMC pipeline transfers to a second MLLM backbone (e.g., LLaVA-1.5 or VideoChat2) to validate backbone-agnostic claims.

key_concerns.issue: Technical novelty of the core operations is limited. The RSA metric is the Fisher / inter-to-intra scatter ratio, a well-known linear discriminant criterion. The anisotropic scaling in Eq. 4 — element-wise multiplication by a context-conditioned vector — is structurally identical to FiLM (Feature-wise Linear Modulation, Perez et al. 2018) and hypernetwork-based modulation. The paper does not cite or differentiate from this literature, making the 'first to operationalize this paradigm' claim insufficiently supported.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Cite and explicitly discuss FiLM and closely related conditioning mechanisms; articulate what the proposed formulation adds over a direct FiLM application (e.g., the residual formulation's stability, the global gate's sparsity bias). This would strengthen, not weaken, the positioning.

key_concerns.issue: The gap to fine-tuned methods on XD-Violence is substantial and unaddressed. Holmes-VAD achieves 90.67% AP vs. SteerVAD's 83.02% — a 7.65-point gap. The UCF-Crime gap (89.51% vs. 87.15%) is smaller but still present. The paper narrates this gap only briefly ('narrows the gap') without analyzing when or why tuning-free methods fall short, nor whether the identified LAEs capture the same phenomena that fine-tuning models exploit.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Provide a qualitative or quantitative failure-mode analysis: which anomaly categories in XD-Violence drive the gap, and does geometric rectification help proportionally across categories? This would contextualize the limitations and guide future work.

key_concerns.issue: The limitations section (final paragraph) is generic boilerplate ('we have not established that conclusions transfer to different architectures'; 'some comparisons are made against a limited set of alternatives') that could describe any paper in the field and does not engage with the specific, identifiable limitations of SteerVAD.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Replace with concrete, method-specific limitations: (1) sensitivity to calibration set class balance; (2) reliance on InternVL3's autoregressive context vector as the global signal; (3) scope of the manifold hypothesis assumption to semantically near-separable anomaly types.

key_concerns.issue: The referenced appendices (A for topological analysis, B for component implementation details, G for further visualizations) are absent from the submitted manuscript, preventing evaluation of the theoretical foundations and implementation specifics that the main text defers to them.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Ensure appendices are included in the submission package. The topological analysis in Appendix A in particular is central to the manifold-hypothesis framing and should be at minimum summarized in the main text.

questions_for_authors: HiProbeVAD is cited as '[Author] et al., 2025' — is this a concurrent or prior submission from the same group? If so, the effective delta SteerVAD claims over prior work is 0.43% AUC / 0.87% AP, which requires statistical justification. Can you provide significance tests comparing SteerVAD and HiProbeVAD across multiple runs?

The anisotropic scaling in Eq. 4 is structurally a FiLM-style affine modulation with a fixed intercept of 1. Can you articulate the specific advantage of this residual formulation over a full FiLM layer (h' = γ ⊙ h + β), and why it is described as a novel geometric transformation rather than a known conditioning mechanism?

Appendix A is described as providing 'rigorous topological analysis' of the representation manifolds and 'detailed geometric interpretation' of Eq. 4. Can you summarize the key topological claims and which of them are theorems vs. informal arguments? Do the manifold structures assumed (compact, smoothly embedded submanifolds) hold for attention head outputs in practice?

Table 3 reports AUC values from 10 seeds ranging from 87.05 to 87.21, with a mean of 87.168, yet the main result in Table 1 reports 87.15%. Is 87.15% one specific seed run, or a rounded mean? If a single run, why not report the mean ± std from Table 3 as the primary result?

The inference description indicates a 'single-forward pass' during deployment, but the full autoregressive pass is triggered post-hoc for flagged segments. What is the end-to-end average inference latency per video segment compared to VERA and HiProbeVAD on the same hardware?
calibration_check: The paper uses carefully hedged language ('competitive performance', 'new direction') and the data-efficiency claim is well-evidenced, but the framing of the theoretical contribution (manifold hypothesis, geometric intervention) significantly overstates the mathematical novelty of element-wise feature scaling — this mismatch between geometric vocabulary and the simplicity of Eq. 4 is the primary calibration concern.

significance.justification: Addresses a real limitation of passive MLLM-based VAD and the data-efficiency angle is practically valuable, but the absolute performance margins over the best tuning-free baseline are narrow and the subfield impact depends on whether those margins hold statistically.

novelty.justification: The application of discriminative head selection and context-conditioned feature modulation to frozen MLLMs for VAD is new, but the RSA criterion is Fisher's discriminant ratio and the HMC is architecturally a FiLM/hypernetwork; the combination is novel but not the components.

rigor.justification: Ablations are well-structured and isolate individual components cleanly, but the causal link between geometric manifold separation (UMAP/t-SNE visualization) and final AUC gains is only shown qualitatively, and theoretical appendices are absent.

statistical_soundness.justification: The seed stability in Table 3 is a strength, but main Table 1 comparisons have no error bars or significance tests, the stability analysis covers only UCF-Crime, and the 0.43% margin over the nearest competitor is almost certainly within noise for a single seed.

calibration_honesty.justification: The data-efficiency and 'competitive' (not best-overall) framing is honest, but the limitations section is generic boilerplate rather than method-specific, and the geometric/manifold vocabulary overstates the mathematical depth of a feature-scaling operation.

clarity.justification: The paper is well-organized and the framework description is readable; notation is consistent and equations are clear, though the manifold hypothesis framing introduces terminology (representation manifolds, geometric entanglement) that is not formally defined in the main text.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard conference structure is followed, but three appendices central to theoretical and implementation claims are absent from the submission, and the limitations section fails to engage with method-specific constraints.

reproducibility.justification: Hyperparameters, optimizer, and hardware are reported; the 1% calibration protocol and K/F selection are described; however, code is not yet available, the backbone InternVL3 version is unspecified, and implementation details deferred to the absent Appendix B.

related_work.justification: VAD literature (traditional, weakly-supervised, MLLM-based) is adequately surveyed, but FiLM and hypernetwork feature modulation literature is entirely absent, which is a notable omission given that Eq. 4 is structurally that mechanism.

figure_quality.justification: Based on captions: the 3D UMAP manifold visualizations and t-SNE before/after rectification plots are directly relevant to the claims and would be informative if rendered; the framework overview (Figure 3) caption describes a clear pipeline diagram.

breadth_generality.justification: Only two benchmarks and one MLLM backbone are evaluated; the paper makes broad claims about a 'new direction' for frozen foundation model adaptation, but no cross-architecture or cross-domain evidence is provided to support generality beyond InternVL3 on UCF-Crime/XD-Violence.

overall_recommendation.justification: Borderline: the concept is sound and the data-efficiency claim is well-supported, but statistical significance of main results is undemonstrated, technical novelty is incremental, evaluation breadth is narrow, and the improvements over the strongest baseline are within likely noise — revision is needed before this crosses the ICLR acceptance bar.
